tagline: 365 Guna-governed Caribbean islands an hour from Panama City — today reached by 4x4-plus-panga over a brutal mountain road, begging for a clean water corridor.
summary: Guna Yala (San Blas) is a self-governed comarca of ~365 white-sand Caribbean islands strung along Panama's northeast coast. It is one of the Americas' most pristine archipelagos and a fast-growing eco-luxury and backpacker destination, yet access is famously painful: a 2-3 hour 4x4 transfer from Panama City to the Cartí dock, then an open panga in exposed Caribbean swell. Inter-island movement is entirely by small outboard launch operated by Guna communities. A foiling-electric layer offers a transformational fit — silent, zero-wake transit that respects the comarca's conservation ethos and Guna sovereignty, collapses island-to-island transfers, and (with Quanta LR) opens a direct sea corridor toward Colón / the Panama Canal Caribbean mouth. Any deployment must be structured as a Guna-partnered operation, not an external concession.

use_cases.title: Guna-operated inter-island transit
use_cases.body: A community-owned foiling service linking the inhabited cays and visitor islands, replacing wet, exposed outboard pangas with a stable, quiet ride that keeps revenue and operation in Guna hands.

use_cases.title: Eco-luxury resort & island transfers
use_cases.body: Silent, zero-wake transfers between the mainland gateway and the island lodges, aligned with the comarca's conservation ethos and far gentler on reefs than diesel launches.

use_cases.title: Cartí & El Porvenir expedition day-charter
use_cases.body: Fast, comfortable day-charters out of the Cartí and El Porvenir gateways to the central cays and Cayos Holandeses, turning the exposed panga slog into part of the experience.

use_cases.title: Mainland gateway & coastal corridor
use_cases.body: A hybrid coastal line-haul from the islands toward Portobelo and Colón at the Caribbean mouth of the Panama Canal — a corridor served only by road and air today.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The inhabited inter-island and gateway legs fit the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Cartí to the central cays (~12 nm) and El Porvenir to eastern Guna Yala (~40 nm) — where silent, zero-wake foiling suits a conservation-first comarca and a community-owned operating model.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no shore-charging dependency on remote cays, conquers the exposed open-Caribbean legs Pioneer II should not and opens the coastal corridor toward Portobelo and Colón (~60 nm) at the Canal's Caribbean mouth.

competitive_landscape: Today: Guna-owned outboard pangas and 4x4 land transfers; no scheduled fast-ferry. Greenfield for a clean-transit layer.
seasonality: Dry season Dec-Apr is peak; Caribbean swell makes a stable foiling ride a year-round safety/comfort advantage.
regulatory_note: Operations governed by the Guna Yala General Congress; partnership and benefit-sharing with Guna communities is a precondition, not an option.
precedents: Maldives resort-transfer model (clean inter-atoll transit at scale)
